+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_ss\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_ss))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/	au_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{remark}[Scope of the rigidity statement]
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.
+\end{remark}

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_ss\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_ss))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/	au_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{remark}[Scope of the rigidity statement]
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.
+\end{remark}

   1: \begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
   2: Assume the hypotheses and notation of
   3: Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
   4: pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
   5: \(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
   6: \[
   7:  0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
   8:  \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
   9:  \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
  10: \]
  11: where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
  12: \[
  13:  \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
  14:  \qquad
  15:  \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
  16:         \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
  17: \]
  18: The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
  19: \begin{align*}
  20:  \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
  21:   &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
  22:  V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
  23:   &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
  24:  A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
  25:   &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
  26:        \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
  27: \end{align*}
  28: For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
  29: relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
  30: \[
  31:  \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
  32:  :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
  33:  \Phi\!\left(
  34:   \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
  35:        {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
  36:  \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
  37: \]
  38: is finite, and
  39: \[
  40:  D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
  41:  =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
  42:   +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
  43: \]
  44: Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
  45: \((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
  46: \[
  47:  \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
  48:        -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
  49:  =o(s^{-2r}).
  50: \]
  51: Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
  52: \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
  53: this class.
  54: 
  55: The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
  56: \(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_ss\}}\) with
  57: \(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
  58: \(\theta(|x|/(c_ss))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
  59: on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
  60: \(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
  61: family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
  62: \end{unnumberedproposition}
  63: 
  64: \begin{proof}
  65: Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
  66: of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
  67: \(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
  68: subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
  69: \[
  70:  q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
  71:   +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
  72: \]
  73: where
  74: \begin{align*}
  75:  R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
  76:  &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
  77:    \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
  78:                   \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
  79:  &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
  80:                   \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
  81: \end{align*}
  82: On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
  83: used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
  84: \(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
  85: sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
  86: remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
  87: vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
  88: dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
  89: convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
  90: condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
  91: \[
  92:  \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
  93:              \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
  94:  +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
  95:              \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
  96:  \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
  97: \]
  98: It follows that
  99: \[
 100:  \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
 101:  \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
 102: \]
 103: The same tail estimate yields
 104: \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
 105: 
 106: Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
 107: \(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
 108: \(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
 109: =\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
 110: mean.  Moreover,
 111: \[
 112:  \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
 113:  \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
 114:        \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
 115: \]
 116: The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
 117: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
 118: \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
 119: \(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/	au_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
 120: \[
 121:  \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
 122:  \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
 123:  \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
 124:               \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
 125: \]
 126: The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
 127: inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
 128: \(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
 129: entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
 130: 
 131: Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
 132: \[
 133:  A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
 134:  A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
 135:  B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
 136: \]
 137: The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
 138: gauge cancel, so
 139: \[
 140:  \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
 141:  \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
 142: \]
 143: All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
 144: \((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
 145: exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
 146: Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
 147: \(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
 148: \end{proof}
 149: 
 150: \begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
 151: Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
 152: proxies of the form
 153: \[
 154:  \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
 155:                          \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
 156:  \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
 157: \]
 158: where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
 159: \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
 160: jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
 161: \(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
 162: \(S_s^\lambda\) such that
 163: \[
 164:  q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
 165:  \qquad
 166:  \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
 167: \]
 168: Then
 169: \[
 170:  H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
 171: \]
 172: is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
 173: \[
 174:  \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
 175:  +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
 176: \]
 177: In particular,
 178: \[
 179:  \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
 180:  +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
 181: \]
 182: Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
 183: common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
 184: law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
 185: one initially writes the normalized proxy as
 186: \(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
 187: normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
 188: \end{unnumberedproposition}
 189: 
 190: \begin{proof}
 191: The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
 192: rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
 193: proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
 194: terms agree, subtraction gives
 195: \[
 196:  s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
 197:    =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
 198: \]
 199: The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
 200: \(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
 201: and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
 202: \(H_s\), and
 203: \(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
 204: \end{proof}
 205: 
 206: \begin{remark}[Scope of the rigidity statement]
 207: The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
 208: order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
 209: ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
 210: it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
 211: for all positive proxy constructions.
 212: \end{remark}

+This tail-proxy entropy is robust at its full resolution: replacing the hard
+cutoff at \(s\) by any uniformly comparable hard or smooth cutoff, allowing
+arbitrary transitions in a fixed scaled annulus, and adding any common

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_ss\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_ss))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/	au_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{remark}[Scope of the rigidity statement]
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.
+\end{remark}

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_ss\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_ss))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_ss\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_ss))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_ss\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_ss))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

+This tail-proxy entropy is robust at its full resolution: replacing the hard
+cutoff at \(s\) by any uniformly comparable hard or smooth cutoff, allowing
+arbitrary transitions in a fixed scaled annulus, and adding any common

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_ss\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_ss))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

+This tail-proxy entropy is robust at its full resolution: replacing the hard
+cutoff at \(s\) by any uniformly comparable hard or smooth cutoff, allowing
+arbitrary transitions in a fixed scaled annulus, and adding any common
+bounded zero-mass order-\(r\) proxy gauge changes it only by

+jet modulo precisely that gauge.

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_ss\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_ss))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.
