+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_ss\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_ss))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

 \input{sec_arbitrary_order_tail_defect_corollaries}
+\input{sec_tail_proxy_convention_robustness}
This tail-proxy entropy is robust at its full resolution: replacing the hard
cutoff at \(s\) by any uniformly comparable hard or smooth cutoff, allowing
arbitrary transitions in a fixed scaled annulus, and adding any common
bounded zero-mass order-\(r\) proxy gauge changes it only by
\(o(s^{-2r})\).  Hence neither the exact vanishing criterion nor
\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) depends on those conventions.  Within
the retained raw-tail/common-core ansatz, normalization forces the tail-mass
subtraction exactly, while order-\(r\) jet fidelity forces the common lower
jet modulo precisely that gauge.

\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
Assume the hypotheses and notation of
Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
\[
 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
 \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
 \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
\]
where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
\[
 \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
 \qquad
 \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
\]
The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
\begin{align*}
 \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
 V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
 A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
\end{align*}
For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
\[
 \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
 :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
 \Phi\!\left(
  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
 \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
\]
is finite, and
\[
 D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
\]
Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
\[
 \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
 =o(s^{-2r}).
\]
Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
this class.

The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_ss\}}\) with
\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
\(\theta(|x|/(c_ss))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
\end{unnumberedproposition}

\begin{proof}
Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
\[
 q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
\]
where
\begin{align*}
 R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
 &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
 &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
\end{align*}
On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
\[
 \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
 +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
 \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
\]
It follows that
\[
 \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
 \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
\]
The same tail estimate yields
\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).

Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
mean.  Moreover,
\[
 \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
 \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
\]
The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
\[
 \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
 \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
 \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
\]
The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.

Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
\[
 A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
 A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
 B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
\]
The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
gauge cancel, so
\[
 \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
 \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
\]
All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
\end{proof}

\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
proxies of the form
\[
 \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
 \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
\]
where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
\[
 q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
 \qquad
 \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
\]
Then
\[
 H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
\]
is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
\[
 \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
 +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
\]
In particular,
\[
 \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
 +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
\]
Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
one initially writes the normalized proxy as
\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
\end{unnumberedproposition}

\begin{proof}
The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
terms agree, subtraction gives
\[
 s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
\]
The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
\(H_s\), and
\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
for all positive proxy constructions.

+\(o(s^{-2r})\).  Hence neither the exact vanishing criterion nor
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) depends on those conventions.  Within
+the retained raw-tail/common-core ansatz, normalization forces the tail-mass
+subtraction exactly, while order-\(r\) jet fidelity forces the common lower
+jet modulo precisely that gauge.

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_ss\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_ss))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_s\,s\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_s\,s))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_s\,s\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_s\,s))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_s\,s\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_s\,s))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_s\,s\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_s\,s))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

CAYLEY­POISSON ENTROPY AND OPTIMAL STABLE-KERNEL
                                  MOMENT EXPONENTS

                                       ANONYMOUS AUTHOR

Abstract. Arbitrary-order first unmatched moment relative-entropy asymptotics under Gauss-

ian smoothing are due to Chen and Niles-Weed [24], while all-order stable/fractional heat-kernel

density expansions are also prior work [47, 48]. Neither result is claimed as new. For the heavy-

tailed isotropic strictly -stable kernels, 0 <  < 2, we identify the optimal complete-moment

condition that transfers the density expansion through relative entropy. If two laws on Rd

match all tensor moments below the integer order r  1, have a nonzero order-r difference r,

and  have  finite  pr,,d th  absolute  moments,  where            }
                                                   {
                                                        2r(d + )
                             pr,,d = max         r,                  ,
                                                    d +  + 2r

then
                           DKL(p(s,d)  p(s,d)  ) = Q,d,r(r)s-2r + o(s-2r).

The coefficient is an orthogonally invariant positive-definite quadratic form on symmetric order-
r tensors. The endpoint moment is sufficient. When d +  > 2r, every exponent   [r, pr,,d)
fails uniformly even for pairs with finite nonzero r; when d+  2r, the threshold equals r, and
smaller exponents fail only to define r throughout the moment class. Thus the contribution is
the heavy-tailed critical exponent, endpoint sufficiency, and uniform sharpness, not the Gaussian
quadratic mechanism itself.

    At every order r, finite rth moments alone also give a law-by-law decomposition: the universal
quadratic tensor term plus a nonnegative relative -energy between two positive proxies that
retain each law's unexpanded tail beyond the smoothing scale and their common lower-order jet.
To the best of our knowledge, this explicit positive proxy decomposition, with vanishing of its KL
term as an exact necessary and sufficient condition for attainment of the universal coefficient, is
new; no uniqueness or canonicity of the proxy is asserted. The defect is nevertheless unchanged
up to o(s-2r) by comparable hard or smooth cutoff scales and by common bounded order-r
proxy gauges; a partial rigidity result identifies this gauge as the remaining freedom inside the
retained-tail/common-core ansatz. For the Cauchy kernel, the Cayley transform additionally
yields the exact equivalence between finite variance and bounded t4 relative entropy, an all-order
finite Laurent rule for the subsequent coefficients, and a fully justified nonlocal Bregman tail
identity for the moving matched quotient.

   Our increment is the heavy-tailed extension. For 0 <  < 2, the Gaussian/Hermite and

exponent works uniformly over the complete moment class: for d +  > 2r this is analytic

uniform sharpness on pairs with a finite nonzero order-r tensor, whereas for d +   2r the
value pr,,d = r is only coefficient-domain minimality below order r.

   The exact law-by-law interface also holds at every order. Under only finite rth moments

and matching below r, Theorem 4.27 retains the common lower-order Taylor jet and each law's
unexpanded exterior translate mixture in positive densities kr,s, kr,s. It proves

                DKL(p(s,d)   ps(,d)  ) = Q,d,r(r)s-2r + DKL(kr,s kr,s) + o(s-2r).

This tail-proxy entropy is robust at its full resolution: replacing the hard cutoff at s by any
uniformly comparable hard or smooth cutoff, allowing arbitrary transitions in a fixed scaled
annulus, and adding any common bounded zero-mass order-r proxy gauge changes it only by
o(s-2r). Hence neither the exact vanishing criterion nor Q,d,r(r) depends on those conventions.
Within the retained raw-tail/common-core ansatz, normalization forces the tail-mass subtraction
exactly, while order-r jet fidelity forces the common lower jet modulo precisely that gauge. Thus
4  ANONYMOUS AUTHOR

the universal coefficient is attained exactly when the nonnegative tail-proxy entropy is o(s-2r).
At covariance order against the point mass at the common mean this reduces, up to o(s-4), to
the one-sided raw-tail -energy in Theorem 4.25. When d +   4, finite covariance forces that
energy to vanish at the required scale; when d +  > 4, it is a genuinely additional law-by-law
condition. The infinite critical-moment boundary is genuinely different: Theorem 4.3 constructs
two laws with the same smooth multivariate regularly varying tail data and the same covariance,
one attaining the covariance coefficient and the other having unbounded scaled entropy along
a subsequence. Theorem 5.1 gives an asymptotically exact finite-covariance characterization of
this distinction. If k,t denotes the positive Poisson density obtained by adjoining the normalized
quadratic mode t-2b to the matched reference, then

                                   t4Hd(t) = Qd() + t4DKL(ht k,t) + o(1).

Thus attainment of the covariance coefficient is equivalent to the vanishing of the complete
nonlinear proxy defect. This statement requires only finite covariance and does not impose a
density or tail regularity on the original law. The leading multidimensional covariance formula
is deliberately read through this analytic route. Finite covariance alone determines the bounded
quadratic mode b and the algebraic number Qd(), but it does not by itself make Qd() the
coefficient of (1.1). It becomes the leading KL coefficient only after a quotient/existence bridge
is in force, for example the (MPJd,L) + (EXd,L) package supplied here by finite L-moment with
L  d + 1, or the separate second-order quotient criterion stated in Section 3.

   The nearest prior work for the heavy-tailed density estimates is Ishige­Kawakami­Michihisa
[47] and the refined follow-up [48]. For every 0 <  < 2 and weighted moment order K  0,
those works subtract moment-weighted derivatives of the stable heat kernel and prove scaled Lq
and weighted L1 remainder decay for the resulting density expansion, including inhomogeneous
and nonlinear refinements. They do not control the matched density quotient in Lq,d(p1(,d) dy)
or transfer that critical estimate through relative entropy; those are the steps that produce p,d
here. They also do not retain the unexpanded translate mixture beyond the smoothing scale
as the nonlinear entropy energy in Theorem 4.25. In contrast, Chen­Niles-Weed give the direct
Gaussian KL precedent (1.2); the present comparison with the fractional-diffusion literature is
only a comparison of the heavy-tailed analytic inputs and does not erase that priority.

   The novelty claim is correspondingly narrow. Arbitrary-order Gaussian first-unmatched-
moment KL asymptotics are prior work, and all-order stable/fractional density expansions are
prior work. To the best of our knowledge, what is new here is the nonnegative law-by-law de-
composition under stable smoothing into the universal tensor coefficient and the KL divergence
of two explicit positive tail-jet proxies, under only finite r-th moments, with proxy vanishing as
an exact coefficient-attainment criterion. We claim neither that this proxy is unique nor that
it is canonical among possible positive proxy constructions. The robustness and partial rigidity
statements above concern the explicit, non-vacuous convention class just described and do not
assert blanket canonicity or entropy minimality.

   The full domain-closure motivation and comparison with the general two-solution Bregman
calculus are in sec_introduction.tex, the paragraphs preceding "Theorems," collected by
supplement_relocated_support.tex.

Proposition (Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz). Fix an admissible retention pro-
file . Consider positive normalized proxies of the form

      As = 1 + Js + Vs, - s,,                             {, },

where Js is common to the two laws and has zero ,d-mean. Suppose the proxies are order-r
jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes Gs , uniformly bounded in
L, and remainders Ss such that

      qs = As + s-rGs + Ss,  Ss  + Ss 1 = o(s-r).

Then

      Hs := sr(Js - Cr-1,s)

is a common zero-mean family bounded in both L and L1, and

                               Gs - (Br - Hs)  + Gs - (Br - Hs) 1 = o(1).

In particular,
                                Gs - Gs - Br  + Gs - Gs - Br 1 = o(1).

Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the common order-r gauge
already allowed by the robustness result, and the law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced
asymptotically. Also, if one initially writes the normalized proxy as 1 + Js + Vs, + cs with a
scalar counterterm, then normalization forces cs = -s, exactly.

Proof. The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy. For the rigidity statement,
compare the assumed split with the exact split in the proof of the robustness proposition with
H = 0. Since the retained-tail terms agree, subtraction gives

      sr(Js - Cr-1,s) + Gs - Br = sr(Rs, - Ss).

The right side tends to zero in both stated norms. Boundedness of Br and Gs therefore proves
the bounds on Hs and the claimed approximation. Subtracting the two law identities cancels
Hs, and Br - Br = Br , which proves the final display.
                                                                                     

Scope of the rigidity statement. The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
order-r gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core ansatz, or assert that
the proxy minimizes relative entropy. In particular, it is a partial rigidity result and not a
uniqueness or canonicity theorem for all positive proxy constructions.

                            5. The Covariance-Matched Poisson Defect

   Finite covariance determines the quadratic mode but, in dimensions at least four, does not
force the matched entropy to attain the corresponding coefficient. The following result identifies
the complete nonnegative remainder without imposing a tail class or an absolute moment above
order two.

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_s\,s\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_s\,s))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

54                                   ANONYMOUS AUTHOR

   It remains to verify, rather than assume, the hypotheses of the abstract two-background KL
perturbation lemma. Put s = s-r, take

    (A1,s, A2,s) = (As , As ),       (B1,s, B2,s) = (Br , Br),            (R1,s, R2,s) = (Rs , Rs).

The modes Br are bounded by (4.104), and their integrals vanish. The first requested back-
ground estimate follows directly from the common jet and the exact tail normalization:
