+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_s\,s\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_s\,s))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_s\,s\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_s\,s))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_s\,s\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_s\,s))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_s\,s\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_s\,s))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_s\,s\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_s\,s))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

+cutoff at \(s\) by any uniformly comparable hard or smooth cutoff, allowing
+arbitrary transitions in a fixed scaled annulus, and adding any common

+subtraction exactly, while order-\(r\) jet fidelity forces the common lower
+jet modulo precisely that gauge.

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_s\,s\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_s\,s))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

-\gdef \@abspage@last{33}

codex
The robustness theorem holds under the existing finite-\(r\)-moment assumptions, for a broad convention class containing smooth cutoffs and every uniformly comparable scale change \(s\mapsto c_s s\). Item 4 was also reached in the form of a precise partial rigidity theorem, without asserting blanket uniqueness, canonicity, or entropy minimality.

**Robustness Result**

The new proof is in [sec_tail_proxy_convention_robustness.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/sec_tail_proxy_convention_robustness.tex:1), with the article summary updated in [main.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/main.tex:122) and [sec_introduction_proxy_robustness.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/sec_introduction_proxy_robustness.tex:1).

An admissible convention is a pair \((\chi,H)\) satisfying:

- \(\chi_s:\mathbb R^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable and may depend arbitrarily on \(s\).
- There are fixed \(0<a<b<\infty\) such that
  \[
  \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
  \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b).
  \]
- \(H_s\) is common to \(\nu\) and \(\eta\), has zero \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean, and is uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\).

The corresponding weighted retained tail and proxy are
\[
\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(dx),\qquad
V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(dx),
\]
\[
A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
 =1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
\]

This class is non-vacuous and substantially larger than a single alternative. It contains:

- the original hard cutoff \(\mathbf 1_{\{|x|>s\}}\);
- every hard cutoff \(\mathbf 1_{\{|x|>c_s s\}}\) with
  \(0<\inf_s c_s\le\sup_s c_s<\infty\);
- smooth radial cutoffs \(\theta(|x|/(c_s s))\), where \(\theta=0\) near zero and \(\theta=1\) outside a fixed radius;
- arbitrary measurable and nonradial transitions in a uniformly bounded scaled annulus;
- an infinite-dimensional family of common bounded zero-mass order-\(r\) modifications of the proxy form.

For every admissible convention,
\[
D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
=
\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+o(s^{-2r}).
\]
Consequently, for any two admissible conventions,
\[
\left|
\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}
-\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}
\right|
=o(s^{-2r}).
\]

Therefore the exact defect-vanishing criterion and the Hessian coefficient
\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are convention-independent throughout this class.

The proof uses an exact cutoff-dependent quotient split. Uniform annular localization and the finite \(r\)-th moment give both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\) remainders \(o(s^{-r})\); the common gauge cancels from the law-difference mode. The existing two-background KL perturbation lemma then gives the same Hessian for every convention.

**Partial Rigidity**

The partial rigidity result starts at [sec_tail_proxy_convention_robustness.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/sec_tail_proxy_convention_robustness.tex:150).

Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\), and consider normalized positive proxies in the retained-tail/common-core ansatz
\[
\widehat A_s^\lambda
 =1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
\]
where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws. If the proxy is order-\(r\) jet-faithful, meaning
\[
q_s^\lambda
=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
\]
with uniformly bounded \(G_s^\lambda\) and
\(\|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r})\), then
\[
H_s=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
\]
is uniformly bounded and
\[
G_s^\lambda=B_r^\lambda-H_s+o(1)
\quad\text{in }L^\infty\cap L^1.
\]
In particular,
\[
G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}+o(1),
\]
so the law-difference mode and its Hessian are forced asymptotically.

Normalization also forces the scalar counterterm exactly: if the proxy is initially written as
\[
1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda,
\]
then necessarily \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\).

This establishes only the following partial uniqueness:

- the lower common jet is forced modulo a bounded common order-\(r\) gauge;
- the subtraction \(-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) is forced by normalization;
- the law-difference order-\(r\) mode and Hessian are forced.

It does not select a cutoff, eliminate the common gauge, cover proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core ansatz, establish global canonicity, or prove entropy minimality. That limitation is stated explicitly in the manuscript. The blanket non-uniqueness disclaimer remains, now qualified by the proved robustness and partial rigidity statement in [sec_introduction_proxy_scope.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/sec_introduction_proxy_scope.tex:1).

+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
+Assume the hypotheses and notation of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
+pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
+\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
+\[
+ 0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
+ \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
+\]
+where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
+\[
+ \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
+ \qquad
+ \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
+        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
+\]
+The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
+\begin{align*}
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+  &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
+ A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
+\end{align*}
+For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
+relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
+ \Phi\!\left(
+  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+       {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
+ \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+\]
+is finite, and
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
+\((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
+\[
+ \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
+ =o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
+this class.
+
+The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
+\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_s\,s\}}\) with
+\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
+\(\theta(|x|/(c_s\,s))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
+on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
+\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
+family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
+of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
+\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
+  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\]
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
+used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
+\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
+sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
+remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
+vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
+dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
+convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
+condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
+             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+It follows that
+\[
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+The same tail estimate yields
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
+\(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+=\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
+mean.  Moreover,
+\[
+ \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
+       \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
+\eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
+\(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
+              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
+\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
+entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
+
+Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
+\[
+ A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
+ A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
+ B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
+\]
+The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
+gauge cancel, so
+\[
+ \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
+ \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
+\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
+exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
+Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
+Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
+proxies of the form
+\[
+ \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
+                         \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
+\]
+where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
+jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
+\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
+\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
+\[
+ q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
+\]
+is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
+\[
+ \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+In particular,
+\[
+ \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
+ +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
+\]
+Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
+common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
+law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
+one initially writes the normalized proxy as
+\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
+normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
+rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
+proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
+terms agree, subtraction gives
+\[
+ s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
+   =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
+\]
+The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
+\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
+and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
+\(H_s\), and
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
+\end{proof}
+
+\paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
+The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
+order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
+ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
+it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
+for all positive proxy constructions.

The robustness theorem holds under the existing finite-\(r\)-moment assumptions, for a broad convention class containing smooth cutoffs and every uniformly comparable scale change \(s\mapsto c_s s\). Item 4 was also reached in the form of a precise partial rigidity theorem, without asserting blanket uniqueness, canonicity, or entropy minimality.

**Robustness Result**

The new proof is in [sec_tail_proxy_convention_robustness.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/sec_tail_proxy_convention_robustness.tex:1), with the article summary updated in [main.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/main.tex:122) and [sec_introduction_proxy_robustness.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/sec_introduction_proxy_robustness.tex:1).

An admissible convention is a pair \((\chi,H)\) satisfying:

- \(\chi_s:\mathbb R^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable and may depend arbitrarily on \(s\).
- There are fixed \(0<a<b<\infty\) such that
  \[
  \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
  \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b).
  \]
- \(H_s\) is common to \(\nu\) and \(\eta\), has zero \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean, and is uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\).

The corresponding weighted retained tail and proxy are
\[
\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(dx),\qquad
V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(dx),
\]
\[
A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
 =1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
\]

This class is non-vacuous and substantially larger than a single alternative. It contains:

- the original hard cutoff \(\mathbf 1_{\{|x|>s\}}\);
- every hard cutoff \(\mathbf 1_{\{|x|>c_s s\}}\) with
  \(0<\inf_s c_s\le\sup_s c_s<\infty\);
- smooth radial cutoffs \(\theta(|x|/(c_s s))\), where \(\theta=0\) near zero and \(\theta=1\) outside a fixed radius;
- arbitrary measurable and nonradial transitions in a uniformly bounded scaled annulus;
- an infinite-dimensional family of common bounded zero-mass order-\(r\) modifications of the proxy form.

For every admissible convention,
\[
D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
=
\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
+\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+o(s^{-2r}).
\]
Consequently, for any two admissible conventions,
\[
\left|
\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}
-\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}
\right|
=o(s^{-2r}).
\]

Therefore the exact defect-vanishing criterion and the Hessian coefficient
\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are convention-independent throughout this class.

The proof uses an exact cutoff-dependent quotient split. Uniform annular localization and the finite \(r\)-th moment give both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\) remainders \(o(s^{-r})\); the common gauge cancels from the law-difference mode. The existing two-background KL perturbation lemma then gives the same Hessian for every convention.

**Partial Rigidity**

The partial rigidity result starts at [sec_tail_proxy_convention_robustness.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/sec_tail_proxy_convention_robustness.tex:150).

Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\), and consider normalized positive proxies in the retained-tail/common-core ansatz
\[
\widehat A_s^\lambda
 =1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
\]
where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws. If the proxy is order-\(r\) jet-faithful, meaning
\[
q_s^\lambda
=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
\]
with uniformly bounded \(G_s^\lambda\) and
\(\|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r})\), then
\[
H_s=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
\]
is uniformly bounded and
\[
G_s^\lambda=B_r^\lambda-H_s+o(1)
\quad\text{in }L^\infty\cap L^1.
\]
In particular,
\[
G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}+o(1),
\]
so the law-difference mode and its Hessian are forced asymptotically.

Normalization also forces the scalar counterterm exactly: if the proxy is initially written as
\[
1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda,
\]
then necessarily \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\).

This establishes only the following partial uniqueness:

- the lower common jet is forced modulo a bounded common order-\(r\) gauge;
- the subtraction \(-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) is forced by normalization;
- the law-difference order-\(r\) mode and Hessian are forced.

It does not select a cutoff, eliminate the common gauge, cover proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core ansatz, establish global canonicity, or prove entropy minimality. That limitation is stated explicitly in the manuscript. The blanket non-uniqueness disclaimer remains, now qualified by the proved robustness and partial rigidity statement in [sec_introduction_proxy_scope.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/sec_introduction_proxy_scope.tex:1).
